sentences.text: The name Hypsilophodon translates to "Hypsilophus-tooth".
This animal possessed a pointed head equipped with a sharp beak designed to bite off plant material.
A maximum length of 2.3 meters is frequently cited for this creature.
However, Galton concluded in 2009 that the largest femur previously attributed to Hypsilophodon actually belonged to Valdosaurus, reducing the maximum known length to 1.8 meters.
Its rear teeth were shaped like fans.
The first remains of Hypsilophodon were discovered in 1849.
This initial specimen was recovered from the Mantell-Bowerbank block.
The type species Hypsilophodon foxii was formally named in 1869.
Abundant fossils of this dinosaur were found on the Isle of Wight.
Hypsilophodon was a bipedal dinosaur that ran on two legs.
The fifth finger of this animal was opposable and could be used to grasp food items.
There is debate regarding whether the front teeth of Hypsilophodon had a specialized function, as most herbivorous dinosaurs had lost them by the Early Cretaceous.
Huxley originally assigned Hypsilophodon to the Iguanodontidae.
In 1882, Louis Dollo named a separate family, Hypsilophodontidae.
In the modern view, Hypsilophodon is simply a basal ornithopod.
Hypsilophodon is traditionally classified as an early member of the group Ornithopoda, though recent research questions this classification.
Hypsilophodon fossils are found in the Hypsilophodon Bed, a marl layer in the upper Wessex Formation dating to the late Barremian, approximately 126 million years ago.
It lived during the early Cretaceous, approximately 124 million years ago in the Barremian stage, in what is now Europe.
The immediate reception to Huxley's proposal of Hypsilophodon as a distinct genus from Iguanodon was mixed.
It is debated whether Hypsilophodon wielandi is a distinct species or synonymous with Camptosaurus valdensis.
Many studies consider Hypsilophodon wielandi a dubious species, leaving H. foxii as the only valid species in the genus.
Reports suggesting Hypsilophodon was present in the later Vectis Formation are considered unsubstantiated by Galton.
